subject: CHEMISTRY
description: Learn how atomic radius, electronegativity and ionization energy change across and down the periodic table, with two worked examples.
caption: Periodic trends in 7 swipes: radius, electronegativity and ionization energy, with two examples and the radius mistake. Free Chemistry study guide at precisstudy.com/chemistry (no sign-up).

slides.title: PERIODIC TRENDS: UP, DOWN, LEFT OR RIGHT?
ATOMIC RADIUS
slides.note: More protons pull electrons in across. More shells push out going down.

slides.title: ELECTRONEGATIVITY AND IONIZATION ENERGY
slides.note: Strong pull and a hard-to-remove electron go together.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: Which has the larger atomic radius, Na or Cl?
steps: Radius decreases across a period, so Na is on the larger side

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: Which is more electronegative, F or O?

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Atomic radius increases from left to right
points: It only increases as you go down a group.
